'''Leonid Veniaminovich Keldysh''' ({{Langx|ru|Леонид Вениаминович Келдыш}}; 7 April 1931 – 11 November 2016) was a Soviet and Russian [[physicist]]. Keldysh was a professor in the [[Igor Tamm|I.E. Tamm]] [[theoretical physics|Theory]] division of the [[Lebedev Physical Institute]] of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]] in [[Moscow]] and a faculty member at [[Texas A&M University]]. He is known for developing the [[Keldysh formalism]],<ref>
{{cite journal
 |author=L. V. Keldysh
 |year=1965
 |title=Diagram technique for nonequilibrium processes
 |journal=[[Soviet Physics JETP]]
 |volume=20 |pages=1018–1026
}}</ref> a powerful [[quantum field theory]] framework designed to describe a system in a non-equilibrium state, as well as for the theory of [[excitonic insulator]]s (Keldysh-Kopaev model, with [[Yuri Kopaev]]).<ref>
{{cite journal
 |author=L. V. Keldysh and Yu. V. Kopaev
 |year=1965
 |title=Possible instability of the semimetallic state toward Coulomb interaction
 |journal=[[Soviet Physics - Solid State]]
 |volume=6 |pages=2219–2224
}}</ref> Keldysh's awards include the 1975 [[EPS Europhysics Prize]] for his work on condensation of excitons,<ref>{{cite web |title=EPS Europhysics Prize |url=https://www.eps.org/members/group_content_view.asp?group=85187&id=554142 |publisher=European Physical Society |access-date=13 January 2022}}</ref>, the 2009 Rusnanoprize, an international nanotechnology award, for his work related to [[molecular-beam epitaxy]],<ref name=rusanoprize>{{cite web |url=http://forinnovations.org/en/laureates/ |title=Rusnanoprize Laureates |accessdate=2016-08-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160710154247/http://forinnovations.org/en/laureates/ |archive-date=2016-07-10 |url-status=dead }}</ref> the 2011 Evgenii Feinberg Memorial Medal, and the 2015 [[Lomonosov Gold Medal|Lomonosov Grand Gold Medal]] of the Russian Academy of Sciences.<ref>{{cite journal
 |author1=Federico Capasso|author2=Paul Corkum|author3-link=Olga Kocharovskaya|author3=Olga Kocharovskaya|author4=Lev Pitaevskii|author-link4=Lev Pitaevskii|author5=Michael V. Sadovskii
 |year=2017
 |title=Leonid Keldysh
 |journal=[[Physics Today]]
 |volume=70 |issue=6
 |pages=75–76
 |doi=10.1063/PT.3.3605
 |bibcode=2017PhT....70f..75C
 |doi-access=free
 }}</ref> 

Keldysh was a son of mathematician [[Lyudmila Keldysh]]. His uncle, [[Mstislav Keldysh]], was a mathematician and the president of the [[Academy of Sciences of the Soviet Union]]. [[Sergei Novikov (mathematician)|Sergei Novikov]], a mathematician and a Fields medalist, is his step-brother.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mccme.ru/~merzon/mirror/abs-otherdir.html|title=In the Other Direction|last=Sossinsky|first=A. B.|publisher=mccme.ru|accessdate=7 October 2017}}</ref>
